# SEO-177: Assign a stable absolute @id to the site-level node

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

## Statement

The node describing the site as a whole carries an @id that is an absolute URL on the production origin and does not change between deployments, content edits, or template changes.

## Rationale

The identifier is what lets separate pages assert facts about the same site rather than about one site per page, so an identifier that changes breaks the connection retroactively for every page that used the old value.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "has_structured_data"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Derive the identifier from the production origin plus a fixed fragment, declare it in one configuration constant, and reference that constant everywhere the site node is emitted or linked. Do not build it from a content identifier that editors can change.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Collect the site-level node identifier from several routes and confirm every route reports the same absolute value.
- Evidence: `JSON_LD`, `ROUTE`, `FILE`
- Automated check: none.
